territorial_scope.description: A Minnesota statute; the candidates it covers are those seeking federal, statewide, legislative, judicial or local office.

evidence.quote: an individual who seeks nomination or election to a federal, statewide, legislative, judicial, or local office

summary.short: Makes it a crime to disseminate a deep fake, or agree to disseminate one, knowing or recklessly disregarding that it is one, without the depicted individual's consent, to injure a candidate or influence an election, within 90 days before a party nominating convention or after absentee voting starts before specified primaries and elections. Enacted 2023 (Laws 2023, c 58, s 2); amended 2024.
summary.long: Subd. 2 criminalizes disseminating a deep fake, or entering a contract or agreement to do so, knowing or recklessly disregarding that it is one, without the depicted individual's consent, with intent to injure a candidate or influence an election, and within the periods stated in Subd. 2(a)(3). A deep fake is a realistic recording or representation, substantially dependent on technical means, of speech or conduct the depicted individual did not engage in. Penalties under Subd. 3(a): up to five years and/or $10,000 for violations within five years of prior convictions; up to 364 days and/or $3,000 with intent to cause violence or bodily harm; otherwise up to 90 days and/or $1,000. A convicted candidate for state or local office forfeits the nomination or office by supplemental judgment, and convicted individuals are disqualified from appointment to office (Subd. 3(b)-(c)). Subd. 2(b) exempts a broadcaster or cable system disseminating a candidate's deep fake where federal law requires it. Subd. 4 allows injunctive or equitable relief against persons reasonably believed about to violate the section, sought by the attorney general, a county or city attorney, the depicted individual, or an injured candidate.

relations.target_text: Minn. Stat. § 211B.17 (forfeiture of nomination or office)
relations.note: Subd. 3(b) requires a supplemental judgment declaring a convicted state or local candidate has forfeited the nomination or office under this section.
Subd. 3(c) disqualifies a convicted candidate or individual from appointment to the office, in accordance with this section.
Subd. 3(c) refers to the legislature's power to establish qualifications for office under this constitutional article.

thresholds.variable_text: days before a political party nominating convention (dissemination window)
thresholds.value_text: within 90 days before a political party nominating convention
thresholds.measurement: Window measured backward from a political party nominating convention; the dissemination must take place within it
thresholds.consequence: Dissemination within this window, with the other elements of subdivision 2 met, falls within the offence
thresholds.conditions: Dissemination without the consent of the depicted individual; intent to injure a candidate or influence the result of an election; person knows or acts with reckless disregard that the item is a deep fake

thresholds.consequence: Selects the first penalty tier in subdivision 3(a)(1) instead of the tiers in subdivision 3(a)(2) and (3)
